steps.title: Prepare cell culture media
steps.instruction: Make DMEM high‑glucose medium supplemented with 1 mM GlutaMAX and 10 % fetal bovine serum.

substeps.instruction: For 500 mL DMEM high glucose, add 5.5 mL GlutaMAX and 50 mL FBS.

steps.title: Prepare basal media
steps.instruction: Make DMEM high‑glucose basal medium containing 1 mM GlutaMAX and 0.2 % fatty‑acid‑free BSA.

substeps.instruction: For 500 mL DMEM high glucose, add 5.5 mL GlutaMAX and 0.2 g BSA.

steps.title: Prepare DPBS buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare phosphate‑buffered saline with 1 mM MgCl₂ and 1 mM CaCl₂.

substeps.instruction: For 100 mL PBS, add 1 mL of 1 M MgCl₂ stock and 1 mL of 1 M CaCl₂ stock.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Make fresh Lysis Buffer 1 on the day of use and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Combine 250 mM mannitol, 5 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 0.5 mM EGTA, and 0.1 % fatty‑acid‑free BSA.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with KOH.
Add protease inhibitor Complete Mini (1 µL per 100 µL buffer, i.e., 1/100 volume).
Add powdered BSA at the end of preparation.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer 2
steps.instruction: Make fresh Lysis Buffer 2 on the day of use and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Combine 250 mM mannitol, 5 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), and 0.5 mM EGTA.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with KOH.
Add protease inhibitor cocktail set III (1/100 volume).

steps.title: Prepare 18 % Percoll gradient
steps.instruction: Prepare a Percoll gradient for mitochondria‑ER separation.

substeps.instruction: Mix 250 mM mannitol, 5 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 0.5 mM EGTA, 0.1 % fatty‑acid‑free BSA, and Percoll to a final concentration of 18 % (v/v).
Dilute Percoll with Lysis Buffer 1 to reach 18 % Percoll.

steps.title: Prepare lipid extraction reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare solvent mixtures and internal‑standard mixture for lipidomics.

substeps.instruction: Extraction solvent: MTBE : Methanol : Water = 10 : 3 : 2.5 (v/v/v).
Resuspension solvent: 80 % MeOH, 20 % H₂O, 0.2 % formic acid, 2 mM ammonium formate.
Mobile phase A: 0.1 % formic acid, 10 mM ammonium formate, 60 % acetonitrile, 40 % water.
Mobile phase B: 0.1 % formic acid, 10 mM ammonium formate, 90 % 2‑propanol, 10 % acetonitrile.

Internal‑standard mixture (50 µL per sample): 40 µM d18:1/17:0 sphingomyelin (2 nmol), 10 µM d18:1/17:0 ceramide (0.5 nmol), 4 µM d17:1 sphingosine (0.2 nmol), 4 µM d17:1 sphingosine‑1‑phosphate (0.2 nmol), 40 µM 18:1/15:0 d7‑diacylglycerol (2 nmol), 80 µM 14:0/14:0/14:0/14:0 cardiolipin (4 nmol), 100 µM d7‑cholesterol (5 nmol).
Store the internal‑standard mixture at –30 °C.

steps.title: Cool equipment to 4 °C
steps.instruction: Pre‑chill all equipment and consumables before starting the isolation.

substeps.instruction: Cool cell homogenizer, DPBS, rotors (TLA110, sw40Ti, JA‑12), centrifuges, 50 mL and 1.5 mL tubes to 4 °C.

steps.title: Grow L6 cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Culture L6 myotubes until 100 % confluency in fifteen 15 cm dishes per condition.

steps.title: Wash cells and incubate in basal media
steps.instruction: Wash and pre‑condition cells before harvesting.

substeps.instruction: Remove growth media and wash cells three times with room‑temperature PBS (6 mL each wash).
Add 10 mL basal media to each dish and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h in a 95 % O₂ / 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Harvest cells and perform lysis
steps.instruction: Collect cells on ice and lyse with Lysis Buffer 1.

substeps.instruction: Transfer dishes to an ice tray.
Wash cells five times with ice‑cold DPBS, adding buffer gently against the dish wall to avoid cell loss.
Add 4 mL Lysis Buffer 1 to the first dish, scrape cells with a cell scraper, and tilt the dish to pool cells.
Transfer the suspension to a second dish, add 4 mL Lysis Buffer 1, and repeat scraping.
Continue the transfer‑scrape cycle until all fifteen dishes are processed; collect the total volume in an ice‑cold 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Homogenize cell suspension
steps.instruction: Disrupt cells using a chilled cell homogenizer.

substeps.instruction: Spin the collected suspension at 1 500 rpm (300 × g) for 5 min at 4 °C (JA‑12 rotor). Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL fresh Lysis Buffer 1.
Assemble the cell homogenizer and equilibrate with 1 mL Lysis Buffer 1; discard the equilibration buffer.
Load the cell suspension into a 1 mL syringe and pass it through the homogenizer 10 times (back‑and‑forth).
Collect the lysate in a new ice‑cold 50 mL Falcon tube; repeat homogenization for any remaining material.

steps.title: Remove nuclei and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Separate nuclei from the post‑nuclear supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 1 810 rpm (600 × g, rmax) for 10 min at 4 °C (JA‑12 rotor).
Transfer the supernatant (~4 mL) to a new ice‑cold 50 mL Falcon tube; discard the pellet.

steps.title: Isolate crude mitochondria
steps.instruction: Pellet crude mitochondria and keep the post‑mitochondrial fraction.

substeps.instruction: Divide the supernatant into two ice‑cold 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Reserve 1 mL as whole‑cell lysate for downstream assays and store at –80 °C.
Centrifuge the tubes at 8 500 rpm (10 300 × g, rmax) for 10 min at 4 °C (JA‑12 rotor).
Collect the supernatant (post‑mitochondrial fraction) in a new 1.5 mL tube and store at –80 °C.
Resuspend the crude mitochondrial pellet in 1 mL Lysis Buffer 1 by gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Isolate mitochondria‑ER (MAM) fraction
steps.instruction: Separate mitochondria‑ER associated membranes using a Percoll gradient.

substeps.instruction: Layer the crude‑mitochondria suspension onto a polycarbonate ultracentrifuge tube containing 7.9 mL of 18 % Percoll gradient.
Add 3 mL Lysis Buffer 1 on top of the suspension using a p1000 pipette for tube calibration.
Weigh the tube and balance with Lysis Buffer 1 to within ±0.001 g.
Centrifuge at 95 000 × g (rmax) for 30 min at 4 °C (sw40Ti rotor).
Using a 1 mL syringe, aspirate the top band (~2 mL) and dispense 1 mL into each of two 1.4 mL Beckman tubes – this is the mitochondria‑ER (MAM) fraction.
Aspirate the bottom band (~2 mL) and dispense 500 µL into each of four 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes – this is the pure mitochondrial fraction.
Weigh each Beckman tube and balance with Lysis Buffer 1 (±0.001 g).
Centrifuge the MAM tubes at 60 000 rpm for 1 h at 4 °C (TLA110 rotor).
Aspirate the mucous pellet (≈200 µL) carefully with a micropipette and transfer to an Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Wash MAM pellet and prepare samples
steps.instruction: Clean the MAM fraction and ready it for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Wash the MAM pellet three times with Lysis Buffer 2: spin at maximum speed for 15 min at 4 °C (JA‑12 rotor) each wash, discarding supernatant.
Add 50 µL of 5× sample buffer to the washed pellet and bring the volume to 300 µL with 1× sample buffer.
Use the resulting suspension for western blotting or store at –80 °C for lipid extraction.

steps.title: Process pure mitochondrial fraction
steps.instruction: Prepare the pure mitochondrial pellets for downstream use.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL Lysis Buffer 1 to each of the four tubes containing the pure mitochondrial fraction and mix gently.
Centrifuge at 10 000 rcf for 10 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate most of the supernatant (~1.2 mL) and add fresh Lysis Buffer 1 to the pellet.
Centrifuge again at 10 000 rcf for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend each pellet in 300 µL 1× sample buffer (≈100 µL per tube) by repeated up‑and‑down pipetting, or store at –80 °C for lipid extraction.

steps.title: Quantify protein (optional)
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of each fraction using the BCA assay; optional cytochrome and CoQ measurements may be performed as described in the referenced methods.

steps.title: Perform lipid extraction
steps.instruction: Extract lipids from 30 µg mitochondrial protein using MTBE‑based phase separation.

substeps.instruction: In a 2.0 mL safe‑lock tube, add 30 µg mitochondrial protein, 200 µL MS‑grade methanol, and 50 µL internal‑standard stock (prepared above).
Add 850 µL MTBE and sonicate in a cold‑room bath sonicator for 30 min, checking every 10 min to keep the bath cold.
Add 212 µL Milli‑Q water to induce phase separation.
Vortex at maximum speed for 10 s and spin at 2 000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer the upper organic phase to a 5 mL glass tube.
Repeat steps a–e two more times on the lower phase, each time adding 2 mL of the MTBE/methanol/water mixture (10:3:2.5 v/v/v) before sonication.
Combine all upper phases in the 5 mL glass tube and dry the extract overnight in a SpeedVac on a low‑heat setting.

steps.title: Reconstitute lipid extracts
steps.instruction: Prepare dried extracts for LC‑MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL of 0.1 % formic acid / 1 mM ammonium formate in 80 % methanol to the dried residue; cover vials with parafilm.
Vortex for 10 s at maximum speed at room temperature (22 °C).
Centrifuge at 2 000 × g for 10 min to pellet insoluble material.
Transfer 300 µL of the clear methanol extract to a glass HPLC vial and store at –30 °C until analysis.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS lipid analysis
steps.instruction: Separate and detect lipids using a Waters Acquity UPLC C18 column and targeted MS settings.

substeps.instruction: Column: 2.1 × 100 mm, 1.7 µm particle size; flow rate 0.28 mL/min.
Gradient (25 min total): 20 % B (80 % A) hold 0–3 min; ramp to 100 % B from 3–14 min; hold 100 % B 14–20 min; return to 20 % B at 20.5 min; hold 20 % B until 25 min.
Detect lipids in positive ion mode on a triple‑quadrupole or quadrupole‑ion trap instrument using selected‑ion monitoring.

Specific transitions: ceramides, sphingomyelin, sphingosine, S1P as [M+H]⁺ with product ions m/z 262.3, 264.3, 266.3 or 184.1; DAGs as [M+NH₄]⁺ with neutral‑loss of FA; cardiolipins as [M+H]⁺ with DAG‑H₂O⁺ product; cholesterol as precursor 369.4 → product 161.1.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article(s): Diaz-Vegas et al. [2], Mitochondrial electron transport chain, ceramide, and coenzyme Q are linked in a pathway that drives insulin resistance in skeletal muscle, eLife 12, RP87340 (Figure 2, panel C, D; Figure 3, panel C, D). Ceramide species were quantified using targeted lipidomics. N = 3 biological replicates. Control conditions refer to cells with vehicle control for each experiment. Student’s t -test was utilized for comparing two groups, whilst ordinary one-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett’s multiple-comparison test was employed for comparing multiple groups.
